question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 21 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign went live, causing a sudden increase in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at 10:25 UTC, 191 minutes before the change.
This led to a 276% increase in request volume in ap-south.
The increased request volume overwhelmed the system, causing a rise in error rate and latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of search v1.26 to eu-west was the cause.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment was 4 minutes before the change, in a different region.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The typo on the help page caused the change.
ruled_out.reason: The typo was reported 244 minutes before the change, too early to explain the sudden jump.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 243 ms (+78%), with a change point at 2026-03-21T10:25:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1233 per 5 min before, 4638 per 5 min after, +276%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.35% before, 0.75% after, +114%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 10:25 UTC (ap-south; 191 min before the change; record R014; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R017; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R018; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Customer reports a typo on the help page. (auth, ap-south; 244 min before the change; record R012; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
Deployed search v1.26 to eu-west (search, eu-west; 4 min before the change; record R016; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (191 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Implement a more aggressive autoscaler to handle sudden spikes in request volume.
Monitor request volume and error rate closely during marketing campaigns to identify and address sudden spikes.
Optimize the system to better handle the expected load during marketing campaigns.
